title: ADI
bodyHtml:
Alberta Diabetes Institute (ADI) IsletCore

https://www.bcell.org/adi-isletcore.html

The Alberta Diabetes Institute (ADI) IsletCore performs research-based isolation, biobanking, and distribution of human pancreatic islets, associated tissues, and phenotyping data.

Data Types

Information on ADI IsletCore and HumanIslets.com tissue processing, data types and data collection can be found here and here.

Biosamples

High-purity fresh, cryopreserved, or snap-frozen pancreatic islets from human donors with and without diabetes; formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded sections from pancreatic tissue biopsies or isolated islets, with custom fixation available on request; pancreas, intestine, spleen, adipose, lymph node, and blood tissues with custom processing available on request

Cellular Phenotyping

Profiles of static and dynamic insulin secretion response to glucose, amino acid, fatty acid: oxygen consumption; and electrophysiology from human islets

Workflows and Standards

Experimental research protocols for human islet isolation and assessment and for in vivo mouse studies and islet isolation

Donor Information

Comprehensive human donor data, including demographics, body mass index, HLA-A2 status, and HbA1c measurements

Islet Preparation Information

Islet isolation information, percent purity, percent trapped, islet particle index, pre-shipment culture time, dithizone-stained islet images, and sample-based functional study data

Omics

Bulk gene expression (RNA-seq, Nanostring), Pseudobulk gene expression, Single-cell gene expression (patch-seq), Bulk protein expression, Bulk metabolomics, Environmental contaminants

Data and Resources

Explore ADI datasets through HumanIslets.com or PanKbase.

Funding and Acknowledgement

Data and/or analyses from HumanIslets.com funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research, BreakthroughT1D Canada, and Diabetes Canada (5-SRA-2021-1149-S-B/TG 179092) with data from islets isolated by the Alberta Diabetes Institute IsletCore with the support of Alberta Health Services, Trillium Gift of Life Network, BC Transplant, Quebec Transplant, and other Canadian organ procurement organizations with written informed donor consent as approved by the Human Research Ethics Board at the University of Alberta (Pro00013094)

More About the Resource

The Alberta Diabetes Institute (ADI) IsletCore isolates, biobanks, and distributes human pancreatic islets and associated tissues for research purposes. ADI distributes biosamples to >170 international groups to facilitate diverse research initiatives. Through HumanIslets.com, the ADI IsletCore has generated deep cellular phenotyping of pancreatic islets from 547 human donors, and growing, for whom extensive donor and isolation metadata are available. Datasets include islet transcriptomics, proteomics, electrophysiology, mitochondrial function, and insulin secretion phenotypes. Through the HumanIslets platform, data can be downloaded, analyzed, or visualized interactively. Terms of service for use of this platform and its data can be found here.

More About the Team

The ADI IsletCore at the University of Alberta is led by Dr. Patrick MacDonald and an internal governance committee including Tina Dafoe (program coordinator), Dr. Peter Senior, Dr. Rebecca Hull-Meichle, and Dr. Vince Rogers. The HumanIslets consortium includes the groups of principal investigators Dr. Ella Atlas (Health Canada/UOttawa), Dr. Jenny Bruin (Carleton), Dr. Leonard Foster (UBC), Dr. Anna Gloyn (Stanford), Dr. Jim Johnson (UBC), Dr. Francis Lynn (UBC), Dr. Patrick MacDonald (UAlberta), Dr. Erin Mulvihill (UOttawa), Dr. Andrew Pepper (UAlberta), Dr. Bruce Verchere (UBC), and Dr. Jeff Xia (University of McGill). More about ADI IsletCore team members here, and about the HumanIslets consortium here.
